note: What an errand COSTS, per world, in watt-hours (pluggybot issue #15).
DATA, not code, on exactly the terms economy/rewards.json and
economy/cadence.json are: this is a measurement about a world, it wants
re-deriving whenever the world or the errand changes, and a deploy has
to be able to re-point it on a mounted volume without a rebuild --
$PLUGGY_ENERGY=/path/to/energy.json.
MEASURED, NEVER GUESSED. scripts/energy_spike.py is where every number
below comes from: it flies each errand once on an oversized pack and
reports the span the mission loop cannot interrupt. A guessed 0.35 Wh
for a drawing that measured 0.93 once had a robot claim the job at 88 %
and die mid-stroke holding the pen.
WHERE TWO HONEST MEASUREMENTS DISAGREE, THE TABLE CARRIES THE DEARER.
An errand's cost depends on where the robot is standing when it starts,
and the gate's failure directions are not symmetric -- an over-estimate
is a charge the robot did not strictly need, an under-estimate is a
robot dead on the way back -- so the high reading wins.
errandWh       action -> Wh for the whole job. A key may also be
`action:target`, which wins over the bare action where
one target is further than another
defaultWh      what an action with no row costs. Omitted means 'the
dearest measured one here', which is the conservative
reading and the right one for an unpriced errand
exploreWhPerS  exploring is not an errand (it is bounded and
interruptible) but the rate is measured so a slice can
be priced in the overseer's prompt
chargeW        NET watts into the pack on the charger. The default
block's is the rover's slowest press (#376 deleted the
rover): lifecycle.charge_timeout catches a robot on pins
that conduct nothing, and sized off a good charge it
would fire on a slow one that is working
READ THE NUMBERS AGAINST THE PACK: the return-trip reserve is a property
of the floor plan (legs/world.py's RESERVE_WH), and an errand must leave
it in hand where the charged pack funds the dearest job plus the reserve.
The lab's acts (issue #226) end where the act is, 25 m from the dock: a
row is the trip OUT and the act, and the way home is what the reserve
funds -- measured from the loop's far corner, further than the lab.

home_quad.measuredOn: measured 28 Sep 2026 on the quadruped with its arm aboard (issue #405), home_quad, 40 Wh pack, the world's 240 s explore, depth camera drawing: the explore 6.067 Wh over 251.4 s (86.9 W; 84.7 without the arm, #387), the legs' windings and shafts and the arm's two motors off their torques, plus 15.9 W of electronics (fourteen drivers standing by); the dock's 216 W charger into a body lying on its pins, 4.987 Wh in 90 s (199.5 W net). No tool errand: the arm takes no tool yet (`world_config`'s `tools`). The lab's acts, which take no tool, measured 30 Sep 2026 with the arm aboard (issues #403, #419), each from the dock with the plate's place remembered: `find` confirms it by its sign, `press` walks on off the sign: feed 1.770 Wh in 73.8 s, care:feed 1.793, care:toy 1.859, shock 1.750 (its job is not offered on legs; priced so it is one line back). The first find of a fresh map's robot, a search round the lab's address, cost 2.160 Wh in 89.5 s and is not carried; a search after an explore can run its whole 300 s (SimNotes, "The feed on legs"). Company is no `care` act on legs, so no row. Hide and seek (#404), the pair's game, measured 1 Oct 2026 over 14 games on the served pair (`solve.py --feature hide_and_seek --swap`, both maps laid from the true floor): the seeker's role, counting and then searching its own map for the whole 240 s, 6.103 Wh at its dearest (6.00-6.10 whenever the seeking ran out, whatever the start), the hider's walk and rest 0.67-1.73 Wh -- the dearer carried. Time, not the walk from the dock, is what the game costs, so the scenes' own starts are its row. The whiteboards' jobs (#406), measured 2 Oct 2026 the same way: each from the dock with the board's place remembered (the day's explore had seen both), at the dearest figure its kind is offered with (`lifecycle.DEAREST_FIGURE`: the house, the robot, the answer 88) -- the board found, the pen fetched off bay B, the body walked in and lain down in front of the board, its face found by touch, the figure drawn and the pen hung back: on the living room's board draw 2.518 Wh in 187 s, artwork 2.613 in 195, answer 2.448 in 168; on the bedroom's 3.397 in 222, 3.188 in 217, 3.315 in 204. A fresh map's first search for the bedroom's board (506 s) is not carried.
